title: Trump Threatens 'Tremendous Tax' on US Firms Building Data Centers Abroad
excerpt: At a White House news conference after his Asia trip, Trump said American companies will be penalized for building AI data centers overseas — but gave no rate, mechanism or date, and said his own officials had not yet been told.
body:
• President Donald Trump said on Friday that the United States will penalize American companies that build data centers overseas, threatening a "tremendous tax" on firms that do.
  • No policy exists yet: Trump gave no rate, mechanism or start date, and acknowledged he had not yet raised the plan with his own officials.
  • The threat lands on real overseas buildouts — Alphabet has announced $15 billion of data-center investment in Malaysia for 2027 and 2028, and operators such as Equinix and Digital Realty run facilities abroad.
  • For readers, nothing changes today: there is no rule to comply with, no filing to make and no tax to pay until the administration publishes an actual proposal.

President Donald Trump said on Friday that the United States will penalize American companies that build data centers overseas, a move he said is intended to help the US artificial intelligence sector compete with China. Speaking at a White House news conference following his trip to Asia, Trump said he would impose a "tremendous tax" on companies that build data centers abroad, according to Reuters.

"We're not going to allow our companies to build data centers outside of our country. We're not going to allow that to happen."

— Donald Trump, US President

"We're not allowing data centers to go into other countries because China will take all of them, and we're not allowing that to happen," Trump told reporters, according to The Wall Street Journal. "And we're going to put tremendous penalties on companies that try and do it." Data centers are critical to the AI boom because they provide the computing power needed to train and run increasingly complex AI systems, and a penalty could complicate the global AI buildout.

Who would be affected

The companies in the frame are the ones financing the global AI buildout. Amazon, Google, Microsoft and OpenAI are pledging billions of dollars to develop data centers overseas, hoping to access cheaper land, labor and electricity while bypassing the local permitting battles that are snarling development in the US, The Wall Street Journal reported. Reuters named Equinix and Digital Realty among the major American data center developers that build and operate facilities outside the US. Earlier this month, Alphabet announced plans to invest $15 billion into data-center infrastructure in Malaysia in 2027 and 2028, according to Dow Jones reporting. Trump argued that if companies will not build in Texas or California, they should build in places such as West Virginia instead.

What has actually been announced

So far, only an intention. The announcement came without details of how the policy would operate, and it is not clear what legal authority the administration could use to penalize companies for building international projects. The Associated Press reported that Trump said he had not yet told his own officials about the plan. "I haven't even said that to my people," he acknowledged. "I'm telling them now — they're here, many of them are here."

A related policy did move this week through formal channels. The Commerce Department moved on Monday to restrict exports of advanced AI chips to several Southeast Asian countries, part of a broader effort to prevent China from obtaining the technology through third countries, Reuters reported. Under the interim rule described by TechCrunch, companies will need licenses to export, reexport or transfer AI chips and servers to data centers anywhere in the world if they may provide compute to companies in China or other restricted countries. The United States already bars direct sales of the most advanced AI chips to China, but Chinese companies have continued to access them by renting computing capacity at data centers in countries that can legally import the chips.

The politics at home

Trump paired the overseas threat with a pitch to American communities that are resisting data centers near them. Politicians across the US are vowing to pause data-center construction amid growing wariness from voters, and in the November 2026 midterms the answer in at least 44 contests was to rein in the industry with moratoriums, new regulations or outright bans, according to USA Today, citing the tracking site Data Centers on the Ballot. Trump urged communities to negotiate instead of refusing projects: "You ought to take advantage of the data centers. Make them pay you. Make them pay your community, but take advantage. Don't shut them off." On Thursday, the Senate approved a bipartisan energy permitting bill that includes provisions intended to make data centers pay for electricity and transmission upgrades; the measure still needs House approval.

What to watch next

The test is whether a formal proposal follows the remarks — a tax rate, a legal mechanism and a start date would turn a press-conference threat into policy that companies with overseas projects, including Alphabet's Malaysia buildout, would have to price in. Trump also teased a new agreement on international rules for AI during the same news conference, saying he and China's President Xi Jinping had agreed to "do some joint guardrails." Until either takes written form, the operative policy remains the one that already exists: the Commerce Department's chip export controls, not a tax on overseas construction.
